reading.title: Every Contact Leaves a Trace
reading.intro_zh: 本文承接 Lesson 47“从证据做推断”的主题，介绍现代法证科学如何用物理痕迹重建事件。内容改编自美国司法部国家司法研究所（National Institute of Justice）关于痕迹证据的资料，属权威政府来源。

source.title: Trace Evidence — Forensic Science
source.publisher: National Institute of Justice (U.S. Department of Justice)

passage: When a crime is committed, the people involved rarely leave behind a tidy confession. Instead, they leave fragments: a single hair, a smear of soil, a few synthetic fibres, or an invisible film of gunshot residue. Forensic scientists treat these fragments as the foundation of an entire discipline, because they rest on a deceptively simple idea known as Locard's exchange principle. Formulated by the French pioneer Edmond Locard in the early twentieth century, the principle holds that whenever two objects come into contact, each transfers some material to the other. Every contact, in short, leaves a trace. The challenge is not whether the trace exists, but whether investigators are disciplined enough to recover it before it is contaminated or lost.

What makes trace evidence so persuasive is that it does not depend on memory or honesty. A frightened witness may misremember events, and a suspect may deliberately distort the truth, but a strand of fibre transferred from a car seat cannot lie. For this reason, physical evidence is often regarded as more reliable than testimony, provided it is collected methodically and interpreted with caution. Crucially, the evidence itself does not announce its meaning. A pattern of soil or a fragment of glass establishes only that a contact occurred; the investigator must then reconstruct a plausible sequence of events that could have produced it. Modern laboratories deploy sophisticated techniques, from spectroscopy to DNA analysis, to extract conclusions from materials so minute that they are invisible to the naked eye. Yet even the most advanced instruments cannot replace careful reasoning, for the same trace may support several competing explanations, and only rigorous analysis can determine which interpretation the evidence genuinely warrants.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Witnesses are usually more reliable than physical evidence in court.
Forensic science reconstructs events from physical traces left by contact, but only careful interpretation reveals their meaning.
Edmond Locard invented every modern laboratory technique used today.
Most criminals leave written confessions that investigators must decode.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文的核心是：法证科学依据“接触必留痕”从物理痕迹重建事件，但痕迹本身不会说明含义，必须靠谨慎的分析与推断。B 项最全面地概括了这一主旨。

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Locard's exchange principle state?
options: Whenever two objects come into contact, each transfers some material to the other.
Physical evidence is always destroyed within a few hours of a crime.
A confession is the most valuable form of evidence in any case.
Only DNA can prove that two people met at a scene.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中明确指出 Locard 原理认为：两个物体一旦接触，彼此都会把一些物质转移到对方身上，即“接触必留痕”。

questions.question: Why is physical evidence often regarded as more reliable than testimony?
options: Because it is always easier and cheaper to collect than statements.
Because laboratories can produce it instantly without any analysis.
Because it does not depend on memory or honesty and cannot deliberately distort the truth.
Because witnesses are legally forbidden from speaking in court.
questions.explanation_zh: 文章说证人可能记错、嫌疑人可能故意歪曲，而一根转移的纤维不会说谎；物理证据不依赖记忆或诚实，因此往往被认为比口供更可靠。

questions.question: What can be inferred about the role of the forensic investigator?
options: The investigator's judgment is unnecessary once a trace has been found.
Advanced instruments have made human reasoning obsolete in modern labs.
A single trace always points to exactly one undeniable explanation.
The investigator must supply the reasoning that turns a trace into a plausible account of events.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中强调痕迹本身不会宣告其含义，同一痕迹可能支持多种解释，连最先进的仪器都无法取代谨慎推理；可推断侦查者必须提供把痕迹转化为合理事件叙述的推断。

questions.question: In the final sentence, the word "warrants" is closest in meaning to
options: conceals or hides from view
justifies or supports
weakens or contradicts
delays or postpones
questions.explanation_zh: 原句说只有严谨的分析才能确定证据真正 warrants（支持、证明其合理）的解释。warrant 在此意为“证明…合理、为…提供依据”，故选 B（justifies or supports）。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 47 的“证据与推断”五个句式提升到 B2+：用 is up for sale 引出耐人寻味的背景，用 had been + 过去分词 客观呈现现场被改动的证据，用 must have done 据证据对过去做强推断，用 suggested that...must have... 提出另一种解释，最后用 will not accept...even if... 写出毫不动摇的拒绝。

patterns.title: is up for sale
patterns.source: A public house which was recently bought by Mr. Ian Thompson is up for sale.
patterns.focus_zh: be up for sale 是固定表达，意思是“正在出售、待售”。它常用来制造故事开头的问题：为什么刚买不久又要卖？
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一处房产、企业或藏品正在出售，并补出一个引人猜测、暗示背后另有隐情的背景。
patterns.sample: The grand riverside mansion, once the pride of the family, is up for sale barely a year after its costly renovation was completed.
patterns.tip_zh: 注意介词是 for：up for sale，不是 on sale。on sale 常表示打折或正在销售。

patterns.title: had been blocked / had been moved
patterns.source: The doors had been blocked by chairs and the furniture had been moved.
patterns.focus_zh: had been + 过去分词 用来写“之前已经被怎样了”。这里不先说谁做的，而是先呈现现场证据。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：描述一个场景在你到达前已被人改动——文件、设备、家具或痕迹已被移走、遮挡或调换位置，且暗示有人刻意为之。
patterns.sample: By the time the auditors finally arrived, several crucial files had been quietly removed from the cabinet and the surveillance camera had been turned to face the wall.
patterns.tip_zh: 如果要突出“被堵住”，可以写 had been blocked by...；如果要突出“被挪动”，可以写 had been moved。

patterns.title: must have done
patterns.source: The ghost must have drunk the night before.
patterns.focus_zh: must have done 不是“必须做”，而是根据证据推断“过去一定做过”。这课里它让同一组证据变成不同解释。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：依据一个具体而微妙的证据，对某人过去一定做过（或未做）某事进行有把握的推断。
patterns.sample: The thin layer of dust on the keyboard was completely undisturbed, so whoever altered the accounts must have used a different computer entirely.
patterns.tip_zh: must have 后面接过去分词：must have come, must have moved, must have forgotten。

patterns.title: suggested that ... must have ...
patterns.source: I suggested that some villagers must have come in for a free drink.
patterns.focus_zh: suggested that... 用来提出一个可能解释，再接 must have... 表示这个解释很有把握。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：作为分析者，根据现场证据提出另一种解释，句中须含 suggested that 与 must have，并指明所依据的证据。
patterns.sample: Examining the muddy footprints leading away from the window, the detective suggested that the intruder must have escaped through the garden long before the alarm sounded.
patterns.tip_zh: suggest 这里不是“建议去做”，而是“暗示、提出一种解释”。

patterns.title: will not accept ... even if ...
patterns.source: They will not accept the pub even if he gives it away.
patterns.focus_zh: even if 表示“即使”。will not accept...even if... 可以把拒绝写得很强：不是条件不够好，而是再好也不要。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人因某种原则或顾虑而坚决不接受某结论、提议或条件，即使对方给出极有利或看似无可挑剔的条件。
patterns.sample: Having seen how the laboratory cut corners on safety, the senior researcher will not accept their findings even if every result is independently confirmed.
patterns.tip_zh: even if 后面接假设条件，主句写结果：即使这样，结果仍然不变。
